short_title: Seagrass decline and the cost to fishing (2020)
title: Economic impact of human-induced shrinkage of Posidonia oceanica meadows on coastal fisheries in the Gabes Gulf (Tunisia, Southern Mediterranean Sea)
summary: Links the fall in coastal fish catches to the loss of seagrass, which accelerated after phosphogypsum releases began in the mid-1970s. Estimates the fishing loss at about 60 million euros in 2014 and over 750 million euros cumulated from 1990 to 2014.

findings.headline: Fishing losses estimated above 750 million euros (1990–2014)
findings.summary: Coastal fishing loss estimated at about 60 million euros in 2014, with cumulated 1990–2014 loss exceeding 750 million euros; catch decline correlated with seagrass decline.
